cls: Oral EGFR kinase inhibitor targeting exon 20 insertions
pharm: Irreversible oral epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) kinase inhibitor with activity against EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations
tags: Boxed warning: QTc prolongation and torsades de pointes
quick: Take with or without food at the same time each day
Can cause fetal harm; avoid - use effective non-hormonal contraception
Do not breastfeed during and for 1 week after the last dose
No adjustment in mild-moderate; limited data in severe - monitor closely
No adjustment in mild-moderate; not studied in severe - monitor closely
No specific interaction; limit due to additive effects
ECG/QTc and electrolytes, LVEF, pulmonary symptoms, diarrhea, pregnancy status
summary: Mobocertinib (Exkivity) is an oral irreversible EGFR kinase inhibitor for adults with locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations after platinum-based chemotherapy, confirmed by an FDA-approved test. The dose is 160 mg once daily with or without food. It carries a boxed warning for QTc prolongation and torsades de pointes requiring baseline and periodic ECG, electrolyte correction, and avoidance of QT-prolonging drugs. Other key risks are ILD or pneumonitis (permanently discontinue if confirmed), cardiac dysfunction with reduced ejection fraction, severe diarrhea, and embryo-fetal toxicity. Note: the US accelerated approval was voluntarily withdrawn in 2023 after a confirmatory trial missed its endpoint, so availability varies by region.
indications: Treatment of adults with locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations as detected by an FDA-approved test, with disease progression on or after platinum-based chemotherapy

dosage.c: EGFR exon 20 insertion-mutant non-small cell lung cancer
dosage.n: Continue until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity; confirm the exon 20 insertion with an FDA-approved test
dosage.t: Once daily, with or without food

dosage.d: Withhold for QTc 481-500 msec or a rise above 60 msec from baseline; resume at the same or a reduced dose after recovery to 480 msec or less
dosage.n: Permanently discontinue for torsades, polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, QTc above 500 msec, or recurrent severe prolongation

dosage.d: Withhold immediately for suspected ILD or pneumonitis
dosage.n: Permanently discontinue if ILD or pneumonitis is confirmed (any grade)

dosage.c: Other severe toxicity or dose reduction levels
dosage.d: First reduction to 120 mg once daily, then to 80 mg once daily; discontinue if 80 mg is not tolerated
dosage.n: Withhold for severe diarrhea, cardiac dysfunction, or other grade 3-4 toxicity until recovery, then resume at a reduced dose

admin: Take 160 mg by mouth once daily, with or without food, at about the same time each day
Swallow capsules whole with water; do not open, crush, chew, or dissolve
Obtain baseline ECG (QTc), electrolytes (potassium, magnesium), and left ventricular ejection fraction, and repeat during treatment
If ILD or pneumonitis is suspected (new or worsening cough, dyspnea, fever), withhold drug immediately and evaluate; permanently discontinue if ILD or pneumonitis is confirmed
Use effective non-hormonal contraception (drug may render hormonal contraceptives ineffective) and avoid QT-prolonging or strongly CYP3A-affecting drugs unless directed
moa: Mobocertinib is an oral irreversible kinase inhibitor designed to target EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations. The insertions alter the EGFR drug-binding pocket so that earlier EGFR inhibitors fit poorly; mobocertinib covalently binds the kinase domain and blocks EGFR signaling, inhibiting proliferation of exon 20 insertion-mutant NSCLC cells. At clinical exposures it also inhibits wild-type EGFR, which contributes to diarrhea, rash, and stomatitis, and it affects cardiac repolarization, which underlies QTc prolongation.

absolute: Known serious hypersensitivity to mobocertinib or any excipient
Congenital long QT syndrome or baseline QTc above 470 msec (avoid per labeling)
monitor: ECG (QTc) and serum potassium and magnesium at baseline and periodically
Left ventricular ejection fraction at baseline and during treatment
Pulmonary symptoms for ILD or pneumonitis
relative: History of torsades, significant arrhythmia, heart failure, or severe cardiac disease
Concomitant QT-prolonging drugs or drugs causing electrolyte loss
Active or prior ILD or pneumonitis
Severe renal or hepatic impairment (limited data)
Concomitant strong or moderate CYP3A inhibitors or inducers

preg: Based on its mechanism and animal findings, mobocertinib can cause fetal harm. Verify pregnancy status before starting. Advise females of reproductive potential to use effective non-hormonal contraception during treatment and for 1 month after the last dose; advise males with female partners of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose.
lact: There are no data on mobocertinib in human milk or its effects on the breastfed infant or milk production. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose.
renal: No dose adjustment is recommended for mild to moderate renal impairment. There are limited data in severe renal impairment; use with caution and monitor closely for QTc, cardiac, and gastrointestinal toxicity.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is defined for mild to moderate hepatic impairment; mobocertinib has not been well studied in severe hepatic impairment. Monitor closely and interrupt or reduce for hepatotoxicity or intolerable adverse reactions.

interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction is described; limit alcohol because of additive gastrointestinal and cardiac effects.
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor ECG (QTc), potassium and magnesium, left ventricular ejection fraction, pulmonary status, CBC, and pregnancy status.
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; avoid grapefruit juice (CYP3A inhibitor) unless the oncology team approves.
major: QT-prolonging drugs (e.g., certain antiarrhythmics, antipsychotics, macrolides, fluoroquinolones, methadone, ondansetron) - additive torsades risk; avoid or monitor ECG closely
Strong or moderate CYP3A inhibitors (e.g., itraconazole, clarithromycin, grapefruit juice) - raise mobocertinib exposure; avoid or reduce mobocertinib dose with closer QTc monitoring
Strong or moderate CYP3A inducers (e.g., rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, St John's wort) - lower mobocertinib exposure; avoid
minor: Gastric acid-reducing agents have no major described effect requiring dose change
moderate: Sensitive CYP3A substrates with a narrow therapeutic index (e.g., midazolam, hormonal contraceptives) - mobocertinib may lower their exposure; use non-hormonal contraception
Drugs that lower potassium or magnesium (e.g., diuretics) - worsen QT risk; correct electrolytes

emergency: Syncope, palpitations, dizziness, or irregular heartbeat (QT prolongation or torsades) - seek emergency care
New or worsening cough, dyspnea, chest pain, or fever (ILD or pneumonitis)
Severe or bloody diarrhea with dehydration, or signs of heart failure (breathlessness, leg swelling)
rare: Symptomatic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
serious: QTc prolongation and torsades de pointes (boxed warning)
Cardiac toxicity with decreased left ventricular ejection fraction and heart failure
Severe diarrhea with dehydration and electrolyte loss

monitoring: ECG for QTc and serum potassium and magnesium at baseline and periodically, and more often with QT-prolonging drugs or CYP3A inhibitors
Left ventricular ejection fraction at baseline and during treatment; evaluate new cardiac symptoms promptly
Pulmonary symptoms; withhold and evaluate for ILD or pneumonitis and permanently discontinue if confirmed
Diarrhea, hydration, electrolytes, and skin or mucosal toxicity; pregnancy status before starting
counsel: This drug carries a boxed warning for QTc prolongation and torsades de pointes, which can be fatal: report fainting, palpitations, dizziness, or irregular heartbeat right away
Report new or worsening cough, shortness of breath, chest discomfort, or fever promptly (possible lung inflammation) - the drug is stopped permanently if ILD is confirmed
Diarrhea is very common: keep hydrated, use antidiarrheals as directed, and report severe, bloody, or persistent diarrhea
Take once daily with or without food; if you miss a dose by more than 6 hours, skip it and take the next dose on time - do not double up

Use effective non-hormonal birth control during treatment and for 1 month after the last dose (1 week for male partners with partners who could become pregnant); do not breastfeed during and for 1 week after the last dose
Tell your team about all medicines, including antibiotics, antifungals, seizure medicines, and heart rhythm drugs; avoid grapefruit juice unless your team approves
pk: Target inhibition with daily dosing; tumor responses develop over weeks
Median plasma Tmax about 4 hours after oral dosing
Steady state reached in about 2 weeks with once-daily dosing
Store at 20-25 C (excursions 15-30 C permitted); keep in original container, protect from moisture
pearls: Boxed warning: QTc prolongation and torsades de pointes - correct potassium and magnesium, monitor ECG, and avoid QT-prolonging drugs
ILD or pneumonitis requires immediate withholding and permanent discontinuation if confirmed
Diarrhea is very common and can be severe - start antidiarrheals early and monitor fluids and electrolytes
CYP3A substrate and inducer - avoid strong or moderate CYP3A inhibitors and inducers; use non-hormonal contraception
Note: accelerated approval was voluntarily withdrawn in the US in 2023 after a confirmatory trial did not meet its endpoint; check local availability and guidelines
missed: If a dose is missed by 6 hours or less, take it as soon as remembered. If more than 6 hours have passed, skip the missed dose and take the next dose at the regular time. If vomiting occurs after a dose, do not take an extra dose; resume at the next scheduled time.
overdose: There is no specific antidote for mobocertinib overdose. Manage with supportive care, including continuous cardiac monitoring (ECG for QT prolongation), electrolyte correction, and monitoring for pulmonary, gastrointestinal, and cardiac toxicity. Contact Poison Help (1-800-222-1222).
